import numpy as np
from scipy import stats

MAX_DRIVERS = 4

def design(feats):
    # Check for clinical/cohort variables that might drive outcomes
    clinical_drivers = []
    for i, fid in enumerate(feats.ids):
        if feats.types[i] == 'clinical' or feats.types[i] == 'cohort':
            x = feats.x[:, i]
            corr, p = stats.pearsonr(x, feats.y)
            if p < 0.05:
                clinical_drivers.append((abs(corr), fid))
    
    # Use clinical variable as driver if found
    if clinical_drivers:
        clinical_drivers.sort(reverse=True)
        drivers = [clinical_drivers[0][1]]
        columns = list(feats.ids)
        return Design(
            drivers=tuple(drivers),
            columns=tuple(columns),
            products=(),
            loadings={}
        )
    
    # No clinical driver found - look for top associations
    correlations = []
    for i, fid in enumerate(feats.ids):
        x = feats.x[:, i]
        corr, p = stats.pearsonr(x, feats.y)
        correlations.append((abs(corr), p, fid))
    
    # Sort by correlation strength
    correlations.sort(reverse=True)
    
    # Select top drivers (max 4)
    drivers = []
    columns = []
    
    for _, p, fid in correlations[:10]:
        if len(drivers) < MAX_DRIVERS and p < 0.05:
            drivers.append(fid)
        columns.append(fid)
    
    # Limit drivers to at most 4
    drivers = drivers[:4]
    
    # Simple approach: just use top features without complex interactions
    return Design(
        drivers=tuple(drivers),
        columns=tuple(columns[:10]),  # Limit columns to avoid too many terms
        products=(),
        loadings={}
    )
